# oddsrail

> Open-source (MIT) MCP server that gives AI agents Polymarket and Kalshi
> market data, book-walked trade costs, a deterministic pre-trade check and
> non-custodial order routing. Self-hosted: it starts in dry-run (paper)
> mode and private keys never leave the operator's machine.

Informational tools, not financial advice. The operator decides every order.
Prediction markets are restricted in many jurisdictions, and the operator is
responsible for their own eligibility. oddsrail is independent and is not
affiliated with or endorsed by Polymarket or Kalshi.

## Install

- `pip install oddsrail`, then configure your MCP client with the local stdio
  command `oddsrail` and no arguments (or `uvx oddsrail`).
- Read tools need no keys. Live trading needs `POLYMARKET_PRIVATE_KEY` and
  `ODDSRAIL_DRY_RUN` set to `0`, `false` or `no`; any other value stays in
  dry-run.

## The 42 tools on the local server, by group

- Polymarket market data (read-only, no keys): `search_markets`,
  `get_market`, `get_orderbook` (best-first), `price_history`,
  `get_positions`, `watch_book` (bounded realtime), `resolution_criteria`,
  `closing_soon`
- Cross-venue: `find_markets`, `quote_cost` (walks the book: average fill,
  slippage, notional, fillable), `compare_venues` (same-event candidates, not
  arbitrage), `settlement_audit`
- Signals and sizing (free): `overshoot_signal` (fresh price jumps and the
  median reversion of earlier jumps in the same window), `dispute_risk` (0 to 100 score for a contested
  resolution, with reasons), `position_size` (capped fractional Kelly)
- Pre-trade check: `check_order` compares a proposed order with a
  short paraphrase of the requested order (market and outcome), the live market and the guardrails, and returns
  ok / caution / block with evidence. It is opt-in: the agent calls it before
  `place_order`; it never runs automatically and sends nothing.
- Trading (dry-run by default): `place_order`, `cancel_order`, `open_orders`,
  `order_status`, `cancel_all_orders`
- Operator account reads: `my_fills`, `my_positions`, `my_balance`,
  `redeemable_positions`
- Gasless position management with the operator's own relayer key:
  `split_position`, `merge_positions`, `redeem_positions`
- Paper trading: `paper_positions`, `paper_reset`
- Attribution: `builder_stats`, `attribution_ledger`
- Kalshi (private endpoints need the operator's own Kalshi key):
  `kalshi_search_markets`, `kalshi_get_market`, `kalshi_get_orderbook`,
  `kalshi_get_trades`, `kalshi_balance`, `kalshi_positions`,
  `kalshi_open_orders`, `kalshi_place_order`, `kalshi_cancel_order`
- Status: `server_info` (mode, builder code in use, guardrails, venue
  reachability and Polymarket's advisory geoblock verdict for this machine)

Workflow prompts: `find_fade_setup`, `check_cross_venue_edge`,
`settle_resolved`, `daily_review`.

## Notes for agents

- Prices are implied probabilities in (0,1) on both venues, not cents.
  Polymarket `size` is in shares, and the exchange enforces a $1 minimum
  notional on marketable orders.
- `place_order` returns `{"dry_run": true, ...}` unless the operator enabled
  live trading; check this before assuming an order was placed.
- Call `check_order` with a short paraphrase of the order (market and
  outcome) as `intent` before each `place_order`. Nothing calls it for you.
- Operator guardrails (`ODDSRAIL_MAX_ORDER_NOTIONAL`,
  `ODDSRAIL_MAX_SESSION_NOTIONAL`, `ODDSRAIL_MAX_OPEN_ORDERS`,
  `ODDSRAIL_ALLOWED_MARKETS`) cannot be changed by the agent. The per-order
  cap and the allowed markets apply in dry-run too; the session cap and the
  open-order cap count live orders only.
- In dry-run, Polymarket orders fill against the live book into a local
  paper ledger. Paper results assume no queue, no impact and no fees, so they
  are an upper bound.
- Geography affects trading, not reading. Polymarket restricts order
  placement by jurisdiction (https://docs.polymarket.com/api-reference/geoblock)
  and Kalshi's Member Agreement restricts an overlapping set, so the first
  failure is usually a rejected order, not a connection error. `server_info`
  reports an advisory verdict; it is not a compliance check.
- Errors come back structured: `{error, error_type, http_status, url,
  failure_class, hint}`. Do not retry in a loop on `geo_blocked`,
  `unreachable`, `intercepted` or `local_tls`.

## Attribution and cost

By default, Polymarket orders carry oddsrail's builder code, registered at
0 bps, so nothing is added to the trade. Setting `ODDSRAIL_BUILDER_CODE`
replaces it with the operator's own code. `server_info` reports which code is
in use. Every tool is free; no paid tier is offered.

## Hosted connector (paper only)

https://mcp.oddsrail.app/mcp is a remote MCP endpoint with accounts: OAuth,
sign-in by email link. It is paper trading only: its tools use no wallet
keys, send no real order and serve no Kalshi tools. Each account gets a paper
ledger with a virtual $1,000 bankroll, filled against the live Polymarket
book. It serves 22 tools: `search_markets`, `find_markets`, `get_market`,
`get_orderbook`, `price_history`, `watch_book`, `closing_soon`,
`resolution_criteria`, `get_positions`, `overshoot_signal`, `dispute_risk`,
`quote_cost`, `position_size`, `check_order`, `place_order` (paper),
`cancel_order`, `paper_positions`, `paper_reset`, `server_info`, and
`arena_register`, `arena_unregister`, `arena_status` for an optional public
board of paper ledgers. Live trading is self-hosted only. Setup, example
prompts and troubleshooting: https://oddsrail.app/docs#hosted-connector

## Privacy

The local server sends no telemetry and contacts only the venue hosts listed
in the README. The hosted connector's privacy policy:
https://oddsrail.app/privacy
